notes: Placeholder factor set shipped with the container images so that a first `docker compose up` produces a calculator that answers. Every value in it is a placeholder - open item O-1, the client has not supplied real New Zealand emissions factors. is_mock is true, which is what makes the non-dismissible placeholder-data warning appear on every results view and export. Replace through the admin panel (clone, edit, publish) as soon as real data arrives; this file is never re-applied to a database that already holds a factor set.

constants.note: IPCC AR5, 100-year horizon. Bound to const_GWP_CH4 when a request carries gwp_horizon = 100. No formula in this placeholder set references it yet — the split of the greenhouse-gas factor into its methane component arrives with the client's real data (O-1).
IPCC AR5, 20-year horizon. Bound to const_GWP_CH4 when a request carries gwp_horizon = 20.

The value of the wasted food itself. Open item O-2 closed at contract v1.48, and not by choosing between cost and retail: the value of the food does not enter this formula at all. The client ruled that it is a figure the business states about its own operation, collected and reported as interfaces.md 4.5's money block, which is statistics and never a metric. This constant therefore stays at zero permanently, and the cost metric reports disposal cost and the waste levy only.

formulas.notes: The default form. Upstream is what it took to produce the food; downstream is what its destination does with it, and may be negative where the destination displaces something worse.
Methane released at the destination. There is no upstream methane row in this placeholder set, so the upstream term is zero throughout.
Embedded water. Almost all of it is upstream — the water was spent growing and processing the food, whatever happens to it afterwards.

Disposal cost and the waste levy. The value of the food itself is deliberately not here: O-2 closed at contract v1.48 in favour of keeping it out of the formula, so FOOD_VALUE_PER_KG stays at zero. Raising it in place would understate the benefit of prevention -- see architecture.md 10, 'O-2 is O-7 again, in the constant dimension'.
The mass metric is the quantity entered. It carries no factors, and it is the one metric a reader can check by hand.

downstream.source_note: PLACEHOLDER. A category-specific row: it wins over the generic landfill row below for dairy.
PLACEHOLDER. The generic row — a null food_category means it applies to every category that has no row of its own.

The New Zealand waste disposal levy, NZD 60 per tonne for municipal landfill. This is the one number in the set that is a real New Zealand figure — it is a charge, not an emissions factor. Gate fees and haulage are not included.

PLACEHOLDER, and negative on purpose: feeding surplus food to animals displaces feed that would otherwise have been grown. A negative downstream factor is an offset and charts must render it below the axis.

Zero by construction. `prevention` is the destination for waste that did not happen, so it contributes no downstream impact. Since open item O-7 closed (contract v1.8) the upstream half is zero too — this factor set carries a `prevention` upstream row per (sector, food_category), so both terms of the line value vanish and prevention is the whole 100% offset docs/architecture.md §4.1 describes. A prevention figure from this set is quotable, subject to the placeholder-data warning every figure here carries.

equivalences.name: Passenger vehicles for a year
equivalences.label_template: Equivalent to running {value} passenger vehicles for a year
equivalences.description: The same greenhouse gases an average passenger vehicle puts out in a year of driving, counted as a number of vehicles.
equivalences.source_note: Client, Data sources for impact calculator (2026-08-29): "Passenger vehicles on the road: GHG emissions (t CO2e) / 2.41 (t CO2e/passenger vehicle/year)". Applied per kilogram, so the divisor here is 2,410.
